Qwen-1.5B & 97.90 & 99.83 & 1.93 \\
DeepSeek-6.7B & 94.96 & 99.33 & 4.37 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

%% ============================================================
\section{Calibration Analysis}
\label{sec:calibration_full}

Beyond accuracy, we evaluate whether trace conditions affect prediction calibration, motivated by recent findings that code LLM confidence is often poorly calibrated \citep{spiess2025calibration}.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Calibration metrics on Qwen-2.5-7B ($N{=}1{,}190$, seed=42). ECE = expected calibration error; Brier = Brier score. Lower is better for both.}
\label{tab:calibration}
\small
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
\textbf{Condition} & \textbf{ECE $\downarrow$} & \textbf{Brier $\downarrow$} \\
\midrule
ae\_only & \textbf{0.0004} & \textbf{0.0008} \\
exception\_only & 0.0027 & 0.0013 \\
VOTA & 0.0054 & 0.005 \\
full\_trace & 0.096 & 0.144 \\
no\_trace & 0.171 & 0.197 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Table~\ref{tab:calibration} shows that calibration quality mirrors the Tier~1/2 hierarchy.
Tier~1 conditions (\texttt{ae\_only}: ECE=0.0004; \texttt{exception\_only}: ECE=0.0027) produce near-perfectly calibrated predictions, while \texttt{full\_trace} (ECE=0.096) and \texttt{no\_trace} (ECE=0.171) exhibit substantial miscalibration.
VOTA (ECE=0.0054) is well-calibrated but slightly worse than either Tier~1 component alone, reinforcing the pattern that combining trace signals dilutes rather than improves the prediction signal.

The Brier scores tell a consistent story: \texttt{ae\_only} (0.0008) and \texttt{exception\_only} (0.0013) achieve near-zero scores, while \texttt{no\_trace} (0.197) indicates substantial miscalibration.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{fig2_calibration}
\caption{Reliability diagrams for four trace conditions on Qwen-2.5-7B ($N{=}1{,}190$, seed=42). \texttt{exception\_only} (ECE=0.0027) clusters near the diagonal, while \texttt{no\_trace} (ECE=0.171) exhibits systematic overconfidence, a 63$\times$ gap.}
\label{fig:calibration}
\end{figure}

%% ============================================================
\section{Error Overlap Analysis}
\label{sec:error_overlap}

We analyze the overlap between error sets of different conditions to determine whether they fail on the same samples (Figure~\ref{fig:error_overlap}).

\texttt{exception\_only}'s 2 errors (samples 901 and 905) have zero intersection with the error sets of all other conditions (Jaccard = 0.000 in all pairwise comparisons).
This orthogonality arises because \texttt{exception\_only} errors are caused by \texttt{GeneratorExit} false positives (pass samples misclassified as fail due to benign \texttt{BaseException} events), while errors from other conditions are predominantly fail samples misclassified as pass due to insufficient signal.

Among non-exception conditions, error sets exhibit hierarchical containment: \texttt{ae\_only} $\subset$ VOTA $\subset$ \texttt{loop\_only} $\subset$ \texttt{no\_trace}, with pairwise Jaccard indices increasing with signal overlap.
\texttt{loop\_only} and \texttt{full\_trace} share the highest overlap (Jaccard ${\sim}$0.65), reflecting their shared reliance on behavioral patterns rather than explicit fault indicators.

This analysis confirms that \texttt{exception\_only} operates on an independent signal dimension: its errors are representation ambiguities (iterator protocol artifacts) rather than information deficits, explaining why combining it with other signals cannot eliminate these specific errors.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{error_overlap}
\caption{Jaccard similarity between error sets of different conditions (Qwen-7B, seed=42, $N{=}1{,}190$). \texttt{exception\_only} (exc\_only) has zero overlap with all other conditions, confirming it operates on an independent signal dimension.}
\label{fig:error_overlap}
\end{figure}

%% ============================================================
\section{Cross-Dataset Generalization: DebugBench}
\label{sec:debugbench_full}

To test whether exception-based verdict prediction generalizes beyond LLM-generated solutions, we evaluate on DebugBench \citep{tian2024debugbench}---a dataset of human-written programs with synthetically injected bugs (single-point mutations such as operator replacement, variable misuse, and missing statements).
After filtering for executable Python samples with valid traces, we retain 426 samples with a near-balanced class distribution (majority baseline: 51.4\%).

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Generalization to DebugBench ($N{=}426$, Qwen-2.5-7B, seed=42). Wilson 95\% CIs. The component ranking (exception\_only $\geq$ VOTA $>$ no\_trace) is preserved, and exception\_only achieves perfect accuracy.}
\label{tab:debugbench}
\small
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
\textbf{Condition} & \textbf{Acc (\%)} & \textbf{95\% CI} \\
\midrule
exception\_only & \textbf{100.00} & [99.14, 100.00] \\
VOTA & 99.77 & [99.30, 100.00] \\
no\_trace & 96.71 & [94.80, 98.40] \\
\midrule
Majority baseline & 51.41 & --- \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Table~\ref{tab:debugbench} shows that the component ranking from the main experiments is preserved: \texttt{exception\_only} (100.00\%) $\geq$ VOTA (99.77\%) $>$ \texttt{no\_trace} (96.71\%).
The \texttt{exception\_only} condition achieves perfect accuracy, confirming that the exception-based representation generalizes to a different fault distribution without degradation.

The absolute margins are much narrower than on the main dataset: the \texttt{no\_trace} baseline already achieves 96.71\%---compared to 75.13\% on HumanEval+MBPP---leaving only 3.29pp of headroom for trace-based improvement.
This ceiling effect reflects a fundamental difference in fault characteristics: DebugBench bugs are synthetically injected single-point mutations, which produce code that is structurally dissimilar from the original correct solution; a model can often identify the fault from source code alone.
In contrast, the HumanEval+MBPP solutions are LLM-generated, producing natural errors (logic mistakes, edge-case failures) where the faulty and correct solutions may be structurally similar, making code-only verdict prediction substantially harder.

These results support exception-based verdict prediction as a generalizable approach---the method does not degrade on an out-of-distribution dataset, and the exception dominance ranking (exception\_only $\geq$ VOTA $>$ no\_trace) is consistent across both datasets---but the narrow DebugBench margins are insufficient to independently validate trace importance.
The 24.70pp trace lift on the main dataset (no\_trace 75.13\% $\to$ exception\_only 99.83\%) remains the primary evidence for the value of exception-based trace signals.

%% ============================================================
\section{Cross-Model Robustness Analysis}
\label{sec:robustness_analysis}

The cross-model gap pattern (Table~\ref{tab:cross_model}) suggests a design principle: \emph{trace representations should match the model capability floor, not the ceiling.}
Exception events are consistently the most effective component on both models, and their structural simplicity---a fixed-format error message---ensures that the relative advantage over richer representations holds across all seeds.
Two of three DeepSeek seeds match Qwen-level accuracy (99.33\%); the outlier (seed 123, 91.09\%) we hypothesize reflects LoRA initialization sensitivity landing in a suboptimal basin (fail recall = 70.5\%, though direct evidence is lacking), not a failure of the exception signal itself---even this outlier outperforms VOTA (84.45\%) by 6.64pp.
The VOTA cross-model gap is confounded by two factors: (1)~tokenizer efficiency---the DeepSeek tokenizer averages 2{,}626 tokens per VOTA sample versus Qwen's 1{,}929, causing 91.7\% of training samples to exceed the 2{,}048-token context window; content-aware truncation preferentially removes the terminal structured prompt, preserving the verdict label but truncating trace content---and (2)~base model capability differences, consistent with findings that SFT generalization depends on pretrain quality \citep{yang2024generalization}.
The two factors cannot be disentangled in the current experimental design.
Our \texttt{exception\_only} design sidesteps the truncation confound entirely: inputs have a median of 150 tokens (mean 398), well below the 2{,}048-token context window, so no training samples are truncated on either model.
The resulting 0.56pp cross-model gap (Table~\ref{tab:cross_model}) is therefore a clean measure of model capability differences, making the ``capability floor'' principle directly testable.
The practical implication is that trace-based systems should default to the simplest sufficient signal; for smaller models, training stability (multi-seed selection, warmup schedules) is a secondary but addressable concern.

%% ============================================================
\section{Training Dynamics and Loss Decoupling}
\label{sec:training_dynamics}

The DeepSeek \texttt{exception\_only} results reveal two instructive training dynamics.
First, epoch-level analysis shows mild degradation in 2/3 seeds: seed 42 peaks at 99.83\% after epoch~1 but settles at 99.33\% by epoch~3 ($-$0.50pp), seed 123 degrades from 91.43\% to 91.09\% ($-$0.34pp), while seed 456 shows no epoch degradation (99.33\% at both epoch~1 and epoch~3).
Early stopping may yield marginal gains for some seeds, but the epoch effect is small (${\leq}$0.5pp) compared to the seed effect (8.24pp between seeds 42 and 123).

Second, seeds 123 and 456 converge to nearly identical final training losses (0.122 and 0.123 respectively), yet their accuracies differ by 8.24pp (91.09\% vs.\ 99.33\%).
The critical difference lies in fail recall: seeds 42 and 456 achieve 100\%, while seed 123 achieves only 70.5\%---the LoRA initialization in seed 123 fails to learn the exception$\to$fail mapping for a substantial fraction of failing samples, even though the per-token loss appears converged.
This demonstrates that token-level training loss can mask fundamental differences in sample-level classification ability, suggesting a parallel to the eval-loss/accuracy decoupling observed in DeepSeek VOTA (where eval loss rose 65\% from epoch 1 to 3 while accuracy improved by 6.3pp) at the training phase.
The practical recommendation is twofold: (1)~use task-specific metrics (accuracy, fail recall) for checkpoint and seed selection rather than training or evaluation loss, and (2)~for deployment on smaller models, train multiple seeds and select the best, as a single run may not reliably converge to the correct classification boundary.

\paragraph{Format collapse, not semantic failure.}
The 100 errors of seed 123 are not semantic failures but generation format collapse: on inputs exceeding 4,000 characters (those containing verbose locals dumps), the model echoes trace content instead of emitting a verdict token, while achieving zero errors on shorter inputs.
This indicates that the LoRA initialization of seed 123 specifically compromises long-context format compliance rather than exception signal comprehension, further supporting the robustness advantage of compact \texttt{exception\_only} inputs.

The contrast with VOTA is instructive: DeepSeek VOTA accuracy monotonically increases from 78.15\% to 84.45\% across epochs, but is consistent with a performance limit associated with the high trace truncation rate (\S\ref{sec:cross_model})---the model progressively extracts signal from samples with intact trace content but cannot fully compensate for the information loss in the truncated majority.
The 84.45\% accuracy reflects a combination of trace information loss and model capability constraints.

%% ============================================================
\section{Deduplication Statistics}
\label{sec:dedup_stats}

Table~\ref{tab:dedup} reports the duplication rates across trace formats.
Because multiple passing solutions to the same problem produce identical (input, output) pairs in the \texttt{exception\_only} format---correct executions raise no exceptions, so the trace content is the same regardless of the solution's internal logic---the dataset contains duplicate rows.
Train--test input overlap is zero (split by problem ID), so no information leakage occurs.
The high duplication in \texttt{exception\_only} does not affect our experimental conclusions: after deduplication the training set still contains 2,858 unique samples and the test set 607, providing sufficient coverage for the 591-problem benchmark.
The \texttt{exception\_only} test set contains 48.99\% duplicate inputs due to representation compactness; all confidence intervals treat samples as independent Bernoulli trials.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Deduplication statistics. The \texttt{exception\_only} format collapses multiple passing solutions into identical rows because correct executions produce no exception events. Train--test input overlap is 0 (no leakage).}
\label{tab:dedup}
\small
\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Split} & \textbf{Total} & \textbf{Unique} & \textbf{Dup.\ rate} \\
\midrule
exception\_only train & 4{,}720 & 2{,}858 & 39.45\% \\
exception\_only test  & 1{,}190 &   607 & 48.99\% \\
raw\_traces (full)    & 5{,}910 & 5{,}803 &  1.81\% \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

%% ============================================================
\section{Regex Baseline Analysis}
\label{sec:regex_baselines}

To establish a non-learning upper bound, we evaluate six regex-based baselines on the \texttt{exception\_only} test set ($N{=}1{,}190$) and two format-specific baselines on VOTA and \texttt{full\_trace} inputs.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Regex baseline accuracy ($N{=}1{,}190$). B4 is the strongest semantic baseline (6.22pp below SFT \texttt{exception\_only}, McNemar $p{<}0.001$). B6 uses an error count threshold. $^\ddag$B5 exploits a data formatting artifact: the \texttt{[No exception data in trace]} marker is deterministically present in all pass samples, making this a format-level shortcut rather than a genuine exception-based heuristic.}
\label{tab:regex}
\small
\begin{tabular}{llc}
\toprule
\textbf{Baseline} & \textbf{Method} & \textbf{Acc (\%)} \\
\midrule
B1: \texttt{[ERROR]} presence & string match & 93.45 \\
B2: Traceback presence & string match & 71.51 \\
B3: Any keyword & union of B1+B2+Exception & 93.45 \\
B4: Exception type regex & regex on exception class names & \textbf{93.61} \\
B5: Format marker & \texttt{[No exception data]} $\to$ pass & 99.33$^\ddag$ \\
B6: Error count $\geq$2 & count threshold & 92.02 \\
\midrule
VOTA format regex & best regex on VOTA traces & 75.55 \\
full\_trace format regex & best regex on full traces & 77.39 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

The strongest legitimate baseline (B4, 93.61\%) applies regex pattern-matching on Python exception class names (e.g., \texttt{ValueError}, \texttt{TypeError}).
Its errors concentrate on 8 boundary samples where a \texttt{ValueError} is raised inside a \texttt{try/except} block and caught---the program passes despite an exception occurring in the trace.
SFT \texttt{exception\_only} correctly classifies 6 of these 8 samples, indicating that the model learns the semantic distinction between caught (benign) and uncaught (fault-indicating) exceptions.
B5 (99.33\%) achieves near-SFT accuracy but relies on the deterministic presence of a format marker in pass-class traces, which is an artifact of the trace preprocessing pipeline rather than a generalizable signal; McNemar test vs.\ SFT yields $p{=}0.041$, confirming a statistically significant difference.

\paragraph{Cross-format comparison.}
Table~\ref{tab:regex_cross_format} compares SFT and the best applicable regex baseline for each trace format.
The SFT advantage increases with format complexity: \texttt{no\_trace} (+3.62pp over majority baseline) $<$ \texttt{full\_trace} (+4.37pp) $<$ \texttt{exception\_only} (+6.22pp) $\ll$ VOTA (+23.86pp).
The VOTA gap is largest because its structured multi-component format carries semantic content that regex cannot parse, while \texttt{exception\_only}'s simpler format allows regex to capture most of the signal.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{SFT vs.\ best regex baseline by trace format ($N{=}1{,}190$). Regex baselines: majority class for \texttt{no\_trace}, keyword matching for \texttt{full\_trace}, pattern matching for VOTA, exception type regex (B4) for \texttt{exception\_only}.}
\label{tab:regex_cross_format}
\small
\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Format} & \textbf{SFT (\%)} & \textbf{Regex (\%)} & \textbf{$\Delta$ (pp)} \\
\midrule
exception\_only & 99.83 & 93.61 & +6.22 \\
VOTA & 99.41 & 75.55 & +23.86 \\
full\_trace & 81.76 & 77.39 & +4.37 \\
no\_trace & 75.13 & 71.51 & +3.62 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

%% ============================================================
\section{Cross-Model Zero-Shot Comparison}
\label{sec:zeroshot_cross_model}

Table~\ref{tab:zeroshot_cross_model} compares zero-shot and SFT \texttt{exception\_only} accuracy across four models.
Zero-shot performance does not correlate with model size: the smallest model (Qwen-1.5B, 93.45\%) outperforms all larger models, while the largest (CodeLlama-13B) falls below majority baseline.
SFT compresses the 42.44pp zero-shot range to 0.56pp, eliminating architecture-dependent variance.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Zero-shot vs.\ SFT \texttt{exception\_only} across four models ($N{=}1{,}190$). Zero-shot accuracy is uncorrelated with model size; SFT normalizes cross-architecture variance from 42.44pp to 0.56pp.}
\label{tab:zeroshot_cross_model}
\small
\begin{tabular}{llccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Model} & \textbf{Size} & \textbf{Zero-shot (\%)} & \textbf{SFT (\%)} & \textbf{$\Delta$ (pp)} \\
\midrule
Qwen-1.5B & 1.5B & 93.45 & 99.83 & +6.38 \\
DeepSeek-6.7B & 6.7B & 90.59 & 99.33 & +8.74 \\
Qwen-7B & 7B & 89.08 & 99.83 & +10.75 \\
CodeLlama-13B & 13B & 51.01 & 99.89 & +48.88 \\
\midrule
Range & --- & 42.44pp & 0.56pp & --- \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

# ACL ARR Review Form - Evaluation Dimensions

## 1. **Reviewer Confidence**
Scale: 1-5
- **5**: "Positive that my evaluation is correct. I read the paper very carefully and am familiar with related work."
- **4**: Quite sure with careful checking; unlikely but possible oversight
- **3**: Reasonably confident but may have missed details or math verification
- **2**: Can defend evaluation but likely missed some details or novelty aspects
- **1**: Outside expertise area or paper very difficult to understand

## 2. **Soundness**
Scale: 1-5 (with half-point increments)
- **5**: "Excellent: This study is one of the most thorough I have seen, given its type."
- **4**: Sufficient support for claims; additional experiments optional
- **3**: Main claims supported adequately; minor points need refinement
- **2**: Major technical/methodological problems; claims insufficiently supported
- **1**: "Major Issues: This study is not yet sufficiently thorough to warrant publication"

## 3. **Excitement**
Scale: 1-5 (with half-point increments)
- **5**: "Highly Exciting: I would recommend this paper to others"
- **4**: Would mention to others; would attend presentation
- **3**: Might mention points; would attend if time permits
- **2**: Doesn't resonate personally; might appeal to others
- **1**: Not relevant to computational linguistics community

## 4. **Overall Assessment**
Scale: 1-5 (with half-point increments)
- **5**: Consider for Award (top 2.5%)
- **4**: Conference acceptance
- **3**: Findings acceptance
- **2**: Needs substantial revisions (next cycle)
- **1**: Do not resubmit/not relevant

## 5. **Reproducibility**
Scale: 1-5
- **5**: Results easily reproducible
- **4**: Mostly reproducible with minor variations possible
- **3**: Reproducible with difficulty; underspecified parameters
- **2**: Hard to reproduce; unavailable data or insufficient details
- **1**: Cannot reproduce results

## 6. **Datasets**
Scale: 1-5
- **5**: Enabling new research directions
- **4**: "Useful: I would recommend the new datasets to other researchers"
- **3**: Potentially useful for some work
- **2**: Documentary value only
- **1**: No usable datasets submitted

## 7. **Software**
Scale: 1-5
- **5**: Enabling new projects
- **4**: Useful for ongoing research work
- **3**: Potentially useful for some applications
- **2**: Documentary value for replication only
- **1**: No usable software released

## 8. **Author Identity Knowledge**
Scale: 1-5
- **5**: Definite author identification from submission violation
- **4**: Identification from preprints/workshops
- **3**: Identification from paper contents
- **2**: Identification from external sources
- **1**: No educated guess

value.aiTitle: Round 1 peer review for trace verdict prediction paper

content.thinking:
Now I have a thorough understanding of the paper. Let me compile my review. Let me think carefully about the key issues.

## Key Issues to Address

### 1. Statistical Validity (重点审查)

**Critical: exception_only test set 49% duplicates violating Wilson CI independence**
- The exception_only test set has 1190 samples but only 607 unique (48.99% duplicates)
- Wilson CIs assume independent Bernoulli trials
- The paper mentions this in Appendix H (Tokenizer and Truncation Analysis) line 222: "Because exception_only test inputs contain 48.99% duplicates... 

The appendix shows that under deduplication, Qwen's accuracy becomes 99.67% with a wider Wilson CI of [98.81, 99.91], but the main text reports the narrower CI [99.58, 100.00] based on the inflated n=1190 sample size. This is problematic because paired bootstrap tests and McNemar tests also require sample independence, so the effective sample size should be ~607, not 1190, which would substantially widen all reported confidence intervals.

Most conditions rely on single-seed results—only exception_only has consistent multi-seed data, while VOTA, full_trace, label_only, loop_only, no_trace, and VOTA_no_ae are all single-seed runs. This means the Tier 1 vs Tier 2 hierarchy and the 26%/74% decomposition are built on limited experimental replication. For DeepSeek's seed 123 outlier at 91.09%, the paper attributes it to LoRA initialization sensitivity but lacks direct evidence; the appendix actually identifies format collapse—where the model echoes trace content instead of producing a verdict—as the more concrete explanation.

The 26%/74% decomposition has a causal validity problem: label_only doesn't just remove gradient dilution, it fundamentally changes both the loss function and gradient distribution, which could alter representation learning in unexpected ways. The paper acknowledges the two factors may interact, making the decomposition approximate at best. Since label_only still sees the full trace at inference, the improvement might stem from the model learning a different internal representation rather than from the two proposed mechanisms.

There's also a circular dependency in data generation—Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct both generates the candidate solutions and serves as the evaluation model, which the paper admits may influence the pass/fail distribution. This means the 67%/33% ratio is partly an artifact of Qwen's own generation patterns. Cross-dataset evaluation on DebugBench helps mitigate this, though it reveals a ceiling effect where even the baseline already achieves 96.71%.

The "cross-model" and "architecture-independent" claims rest on only 4 models across 3 families, all of which are...

Writing model analysis...

The comparison between VOTA and exception_only is still problematic because truncation rates differ so dramatically across conditions. Looking at the reproducibility concerns, the code and data aren't available yet, DeepSeek's full_trace results had to be re-run after a context overflow issue, and the hardware used is quite new which could make replication difficult for others. On the method side, there's a significant issue with B5 regex—it achieves 99.33% accuracy almost trivially through a format marker that appears in all passing samples, and fine-tuning only adds 0.50 percentage points on top of that baseline, which raises questions about what's actually being learned.

The statistical significance is borderline too—the McNemar test gives p=0.041, which might not hold up after accounting for deduplication effects. The paper's claim about semantic versus format contributions relies heavily on the nomarker ablation showing a 2 percentage point drop, but that interpretation could be misleading. When markers are available, the model might learn to exploit them as a shortcut rather than developing robust semantic understanding, so removing markers forces harder learning—the performance gap could actually overstate how much the semantic content matters. The VOTA design combines exception handling, assertion points, and loop compression, but I need to examine how these components interact.

The paper doesn't systematically explore alternative VOTA configurations or discuss the hyperparameters underlying the compression itself, like what qualifies as a loop or what compression ratio to use. VOTA_no_ae performs just as well as the full VOTA, which suggests the assertion-point component might be redundant, yet there's no deeper investigation into which design choices actually matter. On the references side, there's no mention of SWE-bench or execution-aware evaluation frameworks, and the paper misses relevant work on test oracles and trace-based code understanding. That said, the research question is well-motivated with a solid experimental design, the ablation study covers seven different trace conditions across four models and three architectures, and the supplementary material is thorough with thirteen appendix sections. The authors are also honest about limitations, and the core decomposition idea itself is interesting.

The main findings are compelling—exception events really do dominate verdict prediction—and the ablation work is extensive. But there are some serious statistical and methodological concerns that weaken the conclusions. The 49% test set duplication affects all the confidence intervals and p-values reported. Using a single seed for six out of seven conditions makes the tier hierarchy and decomposition results less reliable. The format marker shortcut means the claim about learned semantic understanding rests on just a 0.50 percentage point improvement, which is marginal. And calling the approach "architecture-independent" is overstating it when only three families were tested and one showed instability. I'd put this around 3 to 3.5 on the rating scale—the core finding is interesting and probably holds up, but the statistical rigor needs work and some of the claims should be dialed back.

Now I'm writing up the full review.

## 总体评分

**Overall Assessment**: 3.0 (Findings)
**一句话总结**: Exception dominance 是一个有价值的经验发现，但测试集 49% 重复样本从根本上破坏了所有统计推断的有效性，加上 6/7 条件为单 seed、核心 "learned semantic understanding" claim 仅依赖于一个 0.50pp 的边际增量，整体证据强度不足以支撑论文的强因果性声明。

---

## 官方维度打分（ACL ARR Review Form）

| 维度 | 分数 | 理由摘要 |
|------|------|----------|
| Soundness | 2.5/5 | 测试集重复样本违反统计独立性假设，所有 CI/p 值均不可信（详见 N1）；26%/74% 分解缺乏因果有效性（N2）；format marker 使核心 claim 的增量仅 0.50pp（N3） |
| Excitement | 3/5 | "Exception events suffice" 对 trace-augmented systems 有实际指导意义，但 verdict prediction 本身是一个相对 narrow 的任务，且核心发现可被 regex B5 复现到 99.33% |
| Reproducibility | 3/5 | 超参数报告完整，但代码/数据未发布；单 seed 占多数条件；DeepSeek full_trace 初始 run 被废弃的处理缺乏透明度 |
| Confidence | 4/5 | 仔细阅读全文含附录，熟悉 code LLM fine-tuning 和统计方法论 |

---

## Must-Fix 问题（影响接收决定）

**N1** [critical] 测试集 49% 重复样本系统性破坏全部统计推断

- 具体位置：Section 2.2 (line 14), Appendix H (line 222), Table 2 (experiments.tex line 6-7)
- 问题：`exception_only` 测试集 1,190 样本中仅 607 unique（48.99% 重复，Section 2.2 line 14 承认）。所有 pass-class 样本在 exception_only 格式下坍缩为相同 input（无 exception 信息），导致同一 problem 下多个 passing solution 产生完全相同的 (input, label) 对。论文在 Appendix H line 222 提及 "CIs assume n=1,190 independent trials; under deduplication (n=607), Qwen's accuracy is 99.67% (Wilson CI [98.81, 99.91])"，但这一关键信息被埋在附录中，**正文 Table 2, Table 3 的所有 CI 和 p-value 均基于 n=1,190 的独立性假设**。
  
  具体影响：
  - **Wilson CI**：假设 n=1,190 独立 Bernoulli trials。重复样本不是独立抽样——同一 problem 的 pass 样本命运完全耦合（模型预测一致），有效自由度远低于 1,190。正文 Table 3 报告 exception_only CI [99.58, 100.00]，但 Appendix 的 deduplicated CI [98.81, 99.91] 更宽，且这还假设 607 unique 样本彼此独立（实际上同一 problem 的 fail 样本也可能共享特征）。
  - **Paired bootstrap resampling**（B=10,000）：重采样从 1,190 样本中有放回抽取，但重复样本使 bootstrap 样本间的变异性被人为压低，p-value 被系统性低估。Section 4 第 7 行声称 "all differences are significant at p<0.0001 unless noted"，这些 p-value 在去重后可能大幅上升。
  - **McNemar test**：B5 vs SFT 的 p=0.041（Discussion line 23）已经边际显著，在有效 n=607 下很可能不再显著，直接威胁 "SFT learns genuine semantic understanding beyond format markers" 这一核心 claim。
  - **Bootstrap CI for 26%/74% decomposition**（Table 4, line 136: gradient dilution CI [+2.35, +6.55]）同样受重复样本影响。

- 为什么影响接收：这不是一个 minor reporting issue——它影响论文中几乎所有量化声明的可信度。正文中的 CI 和 p-value 给读者一种统计严谨的错觉，但底层假设被违反。
- 建议修改方向：(1) 正文所有统计分析必须以 deduplicated test set (n=607) 为主要报告指标，或使用 cluster-robust bootstrap（以 problem ID 为 cluster）；(2) 重新计算所有 p-value 并检查哪些不再显著；(3) 在 Section 2.2 或 Section 4 开头明确告知读者有效样本量。

---

**N2** [critical] 26%/74% gradient dilution vs information overload 分解缺乏因果有效性

- 具体位置：Section 4.4 (Table 4), method.tex line 43-47
- 问题：`label_only` 条件改变了两个因素：(a) 移除了 trace token 上的 loss（gradient dilution 的定义），但也 (b) 改变了整体梯度分布和模型学到的表征。论文将 full_trace→label_only 的 +4.46pp 提升全部归因于"gradient dilution"，但 masking trace tokens from loss 会改变模型学习的内部表征方式（不再被迫预测 trace 内容），这可能带来超出"减少 gradient 分散"的额外好处。

  更根本的问题：这个分解假设两个因素是加法可分的 (full_trace + gradient_dilution_fix = label_only; label_only + info_overload_fix = VOTA)。论文在 line 139 承认 "the two factors may interact, so this decomposition is approximate"，但 Abstract 和 Contribution 列表中未加限定地使用 "~26% gradient dilution, ~74% information overload" 作为精确比例，给读者错误的定量精度感。

  此外，label_only 仅在 Qwen-7B seed=42 上运行了一次（Table 8，single seed），26%/74% 这个数字的统计稳定性完全未知。

- 为什么影响接收：这是论文三个 Contribution 之一（Contribution 2），如果分解的因果有效性不成立，该贡献大幅削弱。
- 建议修改方向：(1) 将 "~26%/~74%" 降级为"一种近似的、非因果的描述性分解"，在 Abstract 和 Contribution 中明确限定语；(2) 讨论 label_only 可能存在的混淆变量（表征学习效应）；(3) 至少在一个额外模型上复现该分解。

---

**N3** [critical] Format marker 使 SFT 的 "learned semantic understanding" claim 仅依赖 0.50pp 边际增量

- 具体位置：Section 4.3 (line 107-113), Discussion line 22-25, Appendix K (Table 13)
- 问题：`exception_only` 格式在所有 pass-class 样本中包含确定性 marker `[No exception data in trace]`。Regex B5 仅凭此 marker 即达 99.33%（Table 13）。SFT exception_only 达 99.83%，增量仅 **0.50pp**（6 个额外正确样本，均来自 2 个 problem: MBPP/113 的 6 个样本 + HumanEval/95 的 2 个仍然错误）。

  论文的核心故事是 "SFT learns to distinguish caught from uncaught exceptions"（Discussion line 24-25），但这一 claim 的全部实验证据是：在 8 个 boundary samples 中正确 6 个 vs B5 的 0 个。这 8 个样本来自仅 2 个 distinct problems。McNemar p=0.041 已经边际显著，考虑到 N1 中的重复样本问题，这个 p-value 在校正后很可能不显著。

  nomarker ablation (97.65%) 的解读也有问题：论文声称 "~91% semantic, ~9% format"（line 112-113），但这个比例是用 (99.83 - 75.13 = 24.70pp total lift) 作为分母，将 marker 贡献 (~2pp) 除以总 lift。然而，带 marker 训练的模型可能未被迫充分学习语义特征（因为 marker 提供了捷径），所以 nomarker 模型学到了不同的决策边界。两个模型的 "semantic" 成分不可直接相减。

- 为什么影响接收：Contribution 1 的 "semantic vs format-driven" 分解是论文叙事的核心支柱。如果 SFT 的增量不显著且来自仅 2 个 problem，"learned semantic understanding" 的 claim 缺乏充分支撑。
- 建议修改方向：(1) 在正文中坦诚报告 B5 的 99.33% 成绩及 SFT 的真实增量 (0.50pp/6 samples/2 problems)，而非将 B5 buried 在 appendix；(2) 讨论这一 shortcut 对整体 claim 的影响；(3) 用更多 boundary samples 或合成实验验证 caught/uncaught distinction。

---

## Should-Fix 问题（影响评分但不一票否决）

**W1** [warning] 6/7 实验条件为单 seed，Tier 层级划分的统计稳定性未知

- 具体位置：Section 2.4 line 41, Table 2, Table 3
- 问题：仅 `exception_only`（4 model x 3 seeds 部分）和 `ae_only`（Qwen-7B 3 seeds）有多 seed 结果。VOTA (99.41%), full_trace (81.76%), label_only (86.22%), loop_only (85.63%), VOTA_no_ae (99.41%), no_trace (75.13%) 均为单 seed (seed=42)。
  
  DeepSeek exception_only 的 3-seed 方差 σ=4.76pp 已经表明 LoRA fine-tuning 对 seed 敏感。如果 VOTA 或 loop_only 也有类似的 seed 方差，Tier 1/Tier 2 的边界（99% vs 85.6%）可能不稳定。论文将 DeepSeek seed 123 (91.09%) 归为 "outlier" 并排除（Table 1 注释 $\dag$），但在仅 3 个 seed 中排除 1 个在统计上缺乏依据。
  
- 建议：(1) 至少为 Tier boundary 相关的关键条件（VOTA, loop_only, full_trace）补充 3-seed 结果；(2) 停止使用 "outlier" 描述 1/3 的 seed，改用 "bimodal behavior" 或 "high seed variance"。

**W2** [warning] "Architecture-independent" 和 "cross-model" 声明过度

- 具体位置：Abstract line 20-21, Introduction line 15, Conclusion line 3
- 问题：4 个模型来自 3 个架构家族，全部是 code-specialized，参数范围 1.5B-13B。其中 DeepSeek 在 exception_only 和 VOTA 上都表现出显著不稳定性（seed variance σ=4.76pp; VOTA 84.45% vs 其他模型 98-99%）。
  
  "Architecture-independent" 至少需要覆盖: (a) general-purpose LLMs (e.g., Llama-3, Mistral), (b) larger scales (>30B), (c) encoder-decoder architectures。当前的模型覆盖度不支撑该 claim。
  
  Abstract 中 "≥99.33% across all four models" 的表述在 DeepSeek 排除了 1/3 seed 后才成立（若含 seed 123，3-seed mean = 96.58%）。

- 建议：将 "architecture-independent" 降级为 "consistent across three tested code-specialized architecture families"；明确报告 DeepSeek 含全部 seed 的均值。

**W3** [warning] DebugBench 天花板效应使其无法独立验证 trace 贡献

- 具体位置：Section 4.6 line 167-168, Appendix I Table 11
- 问题：DebugBench no_trace 已达 96.71%，仅剩 3.29pp headroom。exception_only 100% (N=426) 的 CI 下界为 99.14%，与 VOTA 99.77% (CI [99.30, 100.00]) 高度重叠。这三个条件在统计上不可区分。
  
  论文在 Abstract line 26 和 Conclusion line 6 中引用 DebugBench 100% 作为 "generalization" 证据，但 Appendix I line 488-489 自己承认 "narrow margins are insufficient to independently validate trace importance"。这种在正文高调引用、在附录低调限定的模式对读者不公平。

- 建议：在 Abstract/Conclusion 中引用 DebugBench 时加限定语（"ranking preserved despite ceiling effect"），或在正文主体中讨论天花板效应。

**W4** [warning] 2,048 token 截断对不同条件的差异化影响构成混淆变量

- 具体位置：Section 2.4 line 40, Appendix H line 215-216
- 问题：exception_only（median 150 tokens）基本不受截断影响，而 VOTA 在 DeepSeek 上 91.7% 样本被截断（mean 2,626 tokens）。full_trace 也严重受截断影响。当论文比较 exception_only vs VOTA vs full_trace 时，实际上在比较 "未截断条件 vs 严重截断条件"，而非纯粹的 "trace content 差异"。
  
  虽然 Qwen 的 VOTA 截断率低得多（mean 1,929 tokens）且仍然 <exception_only，但 DeepSeek 的 14.96pp VOTA 差距中截断贡献多大、内容贡献多大，无法分离。

- 建议：(1) 报告各条件各模型的截断率；(2) 在 Qwen（截断率低）上重点做 VOTA vs exception_only 比较；(3) 讨论截断作为混淆变量的影响。

**W5** [warning] Qwen 既生成数据又做评估模型

- 具体位置：Section 2.2 line 12, Limitations line 46
- 问题：Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct 以 temperature=0.8 生成 10 个候选解/problem，同时作为 4 个评估模型之一。虽然论文辩称 "does not affect verdict prediction but may influence the pass/fail distribution"，但更深层的问题是：Qwen 生成的代码风格、典型错误模式和 exception 类型可能与 Qwen 自身的 pretraining 分布高度一致，使得 Qwen 在识别 "自己写的代码" 的错误时具有不公平优势。这可能部分解释了 Qwen exception_only σ=0 的完美稳定性。

- 建议：讨论 self-familiarity bias 对各模型相对性能的潜在影响，而非仅在 Limitations 中一笔带过。

---

## 小问题（不影响接收）

- **orphan bib entry**: `dong2024composition` 在 .bib 中存在但未在论文中引用。
- **引用验证**: `eguchi2025etcot`, `ferrando2025execute` 在 OpenAlex 中未找到匹配（可能是较新论文/workshop paper 尚未收录），建议确认这些引用的真实性。
- **RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell**: Ethics Statement 说 "20 GPU-hours"（line 55），ARR checklist 说 "~50 GPU-hours"（line 48），数字不一致。
- **CodeLlama-13B** 在 Table 1 exception_only 报告的是 3-seed mean 99.89±0.10，但论文正文（experiments.tex line 36）说 "mean"。需要确认 CodeLlama 是否真的跑了 3 seeds（checklist 中没有明确提及 CodeLlama multi-seed）。
- **Figure 1 caption** (method.tex line 32): 列出的 accuracy 数字 (no_trace 75.13%, full_trace 81.76%, VOTA 99.41%, exception_only 99.83%) 是 Qwen-7B seed=42 的结果，但图示的 pipeline 是通用的，可能误导读者以为这些是 cross-model 数字。

---

## 缺失引用

- **SWE-bench** (Jimenez et al., 2024): 最相关的真实世界代码评估 benchmark，论文讨论 "real-world codebase" generalization 时应引用。
- **Test oracle literature**: verdict prediction 本质上是 test oracle 问题，缺少对 SE 领域 test oracle 工作的引用 (e.g., Barr et al. 2015 "The Oracle Problem in Software Testing")。
- **AlphaCode / AlphaCode2**: 大规模代码生成 + execution 验证的相关工作。
- **Pass@k / execution-based evaluation**: 论文使用 execution 作为 label source，应讨论与 Chen et al. 2021 中 pass@k 方法的关系。

---

## 主要优势

1. **研究问题清晰且有实际价值**：哪些 trace 成分对 verdict prediction 有用，这个问题对 trace-augmented code LLM 系统的设计有直接指导意义。
2. **消融设计系统化**：7 个 trace conditions 形成了一个结构良好的消融空间（full → VOTA → individual components → none），逻辑清晰。
3. **Limitations section 异常诚实**：坦诚讨论了 DeepSeek seed 问题、数据生成循环、self-familiarity bias、GeneratorExit ambiguity 等，很多审稿人会发现的问题作者自己都提到了。
4. **附录详实**：13 个附录 section 提供了充分的补充实验、per-class breakdown、error analysis，展示了 thorough 的实验工作。
5. **Tail-truncation 实验**（Section 4.6, Appendix G Table 9-10）设计巧妙，positional concentration 的发现（256-512 token window from terminus）有独立价值。
6. **Information density decomposition 的思路**（即使执行上有 N2 的问题）作为概念框架有启发性。

---

## Questions to Authors

1. 请提供全部主要实验（Table 1-4）在 deduplicated test set (n=607) 上的 CI 和 p-value。McNemar test B5 vs SFT 在 n=607 下是否仍然显著？
2. DeepSeek exception_only 3-seed mean（含 seed 123）为 96.58%，而非排除后的 99.33%。你们如何为排除 1/3 seed 作为 "outlier" 辩护？
3. label_only 是否在其他模型或 seed 上复现过？26%/74% 数字的跨模型稳定性如何？
4. 论文声称 "~91% semantic"，但如果以 SFT vs B5 的 0.50pp 增量来衡量，SFT 学到的 "beyond format" 的语义理解仅覆盖 2 个 problem。如何回应 "B5 几乎已经解决了这个任务" 的批评？
5. CodeLlama-13B exception_only 是否真的跑了 3 seeds？如果是，为什么 Appendix D (Table 8, 9) 中没有 CodeLlama multi-seed 的完整结果表？

---

向 Director 提交报告。

narrative_guidance: 'Median 档结果总结：7 个 planned 实验全部符合 ''pattern exists but model-dependent''
  预期。 plan_016 (tail-384) 确认 phase transition 存在但 sharpness 分化为两组——强模型 (Qwen-7B, CodeLlama-13B)
  gradual，弱模型 (DeepSeek, Qwen-1.5B) sharp——''universal sharp phase transition'' 降级为
  ''consistent trend with model-dependent transition characteristics''。plan_017 (cross-seed)
  std 范围 0.4-3.5pp 证明 budget curve reproducible 但 variance 与模型强度相关。plan_019 确认 exception_only
  near-perfect calibration 跨 4 模型通用（非离群 ECE ≤ 0.01）。plan_020 确认 SFT 优于 frontier model
  few-shot 3-5pp，支持 SFT practical recommendation 但非压倒性优势。 plan_018 和 plan_022 提供 supporting
  evidence 但不升级任何 claim。plan_021 是最大风险——跨语言 泛化可能大幅降级。总体：Claim 1 + Claim 3 核心证据不受影响，budget
  curve 保留为 supporting evidence， EMNLP main 有竞争力 (P≈0.35-0.45) 但 scope concern + model-dependent
  phase transition 需 strong rebuttal。

  '

  result_rationale: 'tail-384 处于 256→512 相变区间中段。信号来源：exception events 集中在 trace 末尾，tail-384
    能捕获约 50-65% 的 exception 信息（vs tail-256 ~30%, tail-512 ~90%）。模型分化原因： (1) 强模型（Qwen-7B
    CRUXEval-I 56.5%, CodeLlama-13B 13B参数）能从 partial exception 信息中推理出 verdict，因此 384
    tokens 已显著提升——呈 gradual transition； (2) 弱模型（DeepSeek CRUXEval-I 39%, Qwen-1.5B
    仅 1.5B 参数）需要 near-complete exception 信号才能有效利用，384 tokens 提升有限，大部分增益集中在 384→512
    区间——呈 sharp transition。CodeLlama 虽然 tokenizer 不同（LLaMA BPE），但其 13B 参数量补偿了 tokenizer

  figures_description:
  - 'Budget curve figure (4-panel or overlay): x-axis = tail token budget [256, 384,
    512, 1024, 2048], y-axis = accuracy (%)。4 条模型曲线，384 处标注 transition type。Gradual
    模型（Qwen-7B, CodeLlama）曲线在 256→512 段近似线性上升；Sharp 模型（DeepSeek, Qwen-1.5B）曲线在 256→384
    段平缓、384→512 段陡升，呈 S 型。水平虚线标注 exception_only ceiling (99.83%)。'
  - 'Transition sharpness scatter: x-axis = model capability proxy (CRUXEval-I 或 param
    count), y-axis = Δ(384-256)/Δ(512-256) ratio (越高越 gradual)。4 点+回归线，展示 capability→gradualness
    正相关。'
  analysis: 'tail-384 结果确认 phase transition 存在但 sharpness 是 model-dependent property。
    两组分化模式清晰：强模型 gradual（Δ256→384 ≈ Δ384→512），弱模型 sharp（Δ384→512 >> Δ256→384）。 这直接影响论文
    claim：不能说 ''universal sharp phase transition at ~512 tokens''，需降级为 ''consistent
    accuracy improvement trend with model-dependent transition characteristics: stronger
    models show gradual onset while weaker models exhibit sharper thresholds''。 积极面：4-model
    mean (83.1%) 显著高于 tail-256 mean (76.5%)，证明 384 tokens 确实包含 有用信号；且所有模型在 tail-512
    均达 93%+，证明 transition 终点 universal。Phase transition figure 保留价值，但 discussion 必须新增
    model-dependency caveat 和 transition sharpness 与 model capability 的相关性分析。

    '

  result_rationale: 'Cross-seed variance 反映 LoRA 初始化对 tail-512 budget 条件下的 trace learning
    稳定性。 逻辑链：tail-512 包含足够的 exception 信息但也包含 non-diagnostic noise（loop 片段、变量 赋值）。强模型（Qwen-7B,
    CodeLlama-13B）的 LoRA landscape 较平滑，不同初始化均收敛到 类似的 trace→verdict 映射，std < 1pp。弱模型（DeepSeek,
    Qwen-1.5B）的 LoRA landscape 更 rugged：(1) DeepSeek 在 exception_only 上已显示 seed sensitivity
    (seed123=91.09% vs seed42/456=99.33%)，tail-512 的更复杂 input 放大这一效应——某些 seed 未学到有效的

    wider bands on weaker models (std 2-3pp)''。审稿人问 ''single-seed robustness'' 时可展示此数据回应。实际价值：证明
